sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。在这个节目中，你可以聆听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the unexpected return of nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge。今天，我们将探讨核能的意外回归。

sentences.en: It's a story about technology, energy, politics, and the question of how to power the future.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于技术、能源、政治以及如何为未来提供动力的问题的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们事不宜迟，直接进入正题。

sentences.en: Politicians don't tend to be particularly good at admitting they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 政治家们通常不太擅长承认自己犯了错。

sentences.en: When your career depends on voters believing that you are the best person to lead the country, saying that you should have done something differently is hard.
sentences.zh: 当你的职业生涯取决于选民是否相信你是领导国家的最佳人选时，要承认自己本该采取不同的做法是很困难的。

sentences.en: It's uncomfortable. Sometimes, though, it happens.
sentences.zh: 这让人很不舒服。不过，这种情况有时确实会发生。

sentences.en: In January of this year, January of 2026, the German Chancellor, Friedrich Merz, stood in front of the Chamber of Industry and Commerce in Dessau and admitted, in no uncertain terms, that his country, Germany, had made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 今年1月，也就是2026年1月，德国总理 Friedrich Merz 站在德绍工商会前，毫不含糊地承认他的国家——德国，犯了一个错误。

sentences.en: To quote him exactly, "It was a serious strategic mistake to exit nuclear energy… we simply don’t have enough energy generation capacity."
sentences.zh: 准确地引用他的原话："退出核能是一个严重的战略错误……我们根本没有足够的发电能力。"

sentences.en: As you may know, Germany now has no active nuclear power plants.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道，德国现在已经没有运行中的核电站了。

sentences.en: In the 1990s, around 30% of Germany's electricity came from nuclear sources.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代，德国约30%的电力来自核能。

sentences.en: Today, that number is zero. And many countries, especially in Europe, have gone a similar route: initial excitement in the post-war period about this "new" and revolutionary technology, and then a turn towards protest and opposition.
sentences.zh: 如今，这个数字是零。许多国家，尤其是欧洲国家，也走过了类似的历程：战后初期对这项"全新"且具有革命性的技术感到兴奋，随后便转向了抗议和反对。

sentences.en: In many ways, it was hardly surprising. There were question marks over what to do with nuclear waste.
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来看，这并不令人意外。如何处理核废料一直存在疑问。

sentences.en: In 1986, there was Chernobyl. And twenty-five years later, in 2011, came Fukushima.
sentences.zh: 1986年发生了切尔诺贝利事故。25年后的2011年，又发生了福岛核事故。

sentences.en: Nuclear power was for many people simply too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，核能实在太危险了。

sentences.en: A risk not worth taking. But then, in the past couple of years, something has changed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不值得冒的风险。但在过去的几年里，情况发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: People have started talking about a new nuclear age, a nuclear renaissance, where nuclear energy is treated not as "the answer" to how we power the planet, but as "part of the answer".
sentences.zh: 人们开始谈论一个新的核能时代，即核能复兴。在这里，核能不再被视为解决地球能源问题的"唯一答案"，而是被视为"答案的一部分"。

sentences.en: And in some cases, this has resulted in some spectacular U-turns.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这导致了一些惊人的态度大转变。

sentences.en: Belgium is one example. In 2003, Belgium passed a law committing itself to shutting down every nuclear reactor in the country.
sentences.zh: 比利时就是一个例子。2003年，比利时通过了一项法律，承诺关闭该国所有的核反应堆。

sentences.en: It was broadly the same story as Germany: public fear after Chernobyl, a strong Green movement, and a political consensus that nuclear power belonged to the past.
sentences.zh: 这与德国的情况大致相同：切尔诺贝利事故后公众的恐惧、强烈的绿色运动，以及核能属于过去的政治共识。

sentences.en: By last year, Belgium was most of the way there.
sentences.zh: 到去年，比利时已经基本完成了这一目标。

sentences.en: Plants had been scheduled for closure. Engineers had already begun the paperwork for decommissioning, which is the long, careful process of shutting a reactor down for good and making it safe.
sentences.zh: 核电站已被安排关闭。工程师们已经开始办理退役手续，这是一个漫长而谨慎的过程，旨在永久关闭反应堆并确保其安全。

sentences.en: And then, in May 2025, the Belgian parliament did something people weren't expecting.
sentences.zh: 随后，在2025年5月，比利时议会做了一件人们意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: It repealed the law completely, cancelling it as if it had never existed.
sentences.zh: 它彻底废除了这项法律，将其取消，就好像它从未存在过一样。

sentences.en: And the government didn't just decide to keep the remaining reactors running.
sentences.zh: 而且政府不仅决定让剩余的反应堆继续运行。

sentences.en: It announced it wanted to extend the lifespans of the ones that had already been prepared for shutdown, and it started looking at building new ones.
sentences.zh: 它还宣布希望延长那些已经准备关闭的反应堆的寿命，并开始考虑建造新的反应堆。

sentences.en: In other words, a full reversal: from "we're shutting it all down" to "we're not doing that AND we're building new ones".
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个彻底的逆转：从"我们要关闭所有反应堆"变成了"我们不关了，而且还要建新的"。

sentences.en: Belgium wasn't even the most extreme example.
sentences.zh: 比利时甚至还不是最极端的例子。

sentences.en: Italy banned nuclear power after Chernobyl, and confirmed that ban again after Fukushima, when 94% of voters rejected building new reactors.
sentences.zh: 意大利在切尔诺贝利事故后禁用了核能，并在福岛核事故后再次确认了这一禁令，当时94%的选民拒绝建造新的反应堆。

sentences.en: Its last two reactors had already closed, back in 1990.
sentences.zh: 早在1990年，它的最后两个反应堆就已经关闭了。

sentences.en: But in October of last year, October 2025, Italy's government approved a new bill to bring nuclear power back: small modular reactors, new-generation designs, and even fusion.
sentences.zh: 但在去年10月，也就是2025年10月，意大利政府批准了一项新法案以恢复核能：小型模块化反应堆、新一代设计，甚至还有核聚变。

sentences.en: The whole shebang. And it's a similar change of mood in the US, in Japan, the world over.
sentences.zh: 样样俱全。在美国、日本以及全世界，人们的态度也都发生了类似的转变。

sentences.en: Even in countries that haven't reversed course entirely, the tone has changed.
sentences.zh: 即使在那些没有完全改变路线的国家，基调也已经变了。

sentences.en: In many countries, nuclear power has become a non-partisan issue: something those on the right and the left agree on, and even something that some Green parties have started to come round to as an important tool in the fight against climate change.
sentences.zh: 在许多国家，核能已经成为一个超越党派的问题：左右两派对此达成了一致，甚至一些绿党也开始转变观念，将其视为应对气候变化的重要工具。

sentences.en: So what changed? Well, first, there's the question of energy security.
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么改变了呢？首先，是能源安全问题。

sentences.en: After the Russian invasion of Ukraine, it became clear that relying on cheap Russian gas hadn't been the smartest move.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后，情况变得很明显，依赖廉价的俄罗斯天然气并不是最明智的举动。

sentences.en: Or in fact relying on anyone else for that matter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，依赖任何其他国家都是如此。

sentences.en: To maintain acceptable prices and reliable supply, countries started to admit that being able to produce your own energy was extremely important.
sentences.zh: 为了维持合理的价格和可靠的供应，各国开始承认，能够自主生产能源是极其重要的。

sentences.en: Second, there's the climate question. For a long time, the assumption was that renewables like wind and solar could be enough.
sentences.zh: 其次，是气候问题。长期以来，人们一直假设风能和太阳能等可再生能源就足够了。

sentences.en: Enough wind turbines and solar panels could deliver all the energy a country needed.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够的风力发电机和太阳能电池板，就能提供一个国家所需的全部能源。

sentences.en: It's a nice idea, but for most countries, it doesn't quite work.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的想法，但对大多数国家来说，这并不太行得通。

sentences.en: Wind and solar are cheap, and they are quick and easy to build, relative to nuclear at least.
sentences.zh: 风能和太阳能很便宜，而且建造起来又快又容易，至少相对于核能是这样。

sentences.en: But the sun doesn't always shine, and the wind doesn't always blow.
sentences.zh: 但太阳并不总是照耀，风也并不总是吹拂。

sentences.en: Solar might be able to power the entire grid in the middle of the day, but not at night or on a dark winter's day.
sentences.zh: 太阳能也许能在中午为整个电网供电，但在夜间或阴暗的冬日却无能为力。

sentences.en: And while batteries are getting cheaper every year, storing enough electricity to keep a country running for days at a time is still a long way off.
sentences.zh: 虽然电池每年都在变得更便宜，但要储存足够的电量来维持一个国家连续运行数天，依然还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: Nuclear power, on the other hand, doesn't care whether the sun is shining or the wind is blowing.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，核能并不在乎太阳是否在照耀，也不在乎风是否在吹拂。

sentences.en: Grid engineers call this baseload power: a steady, reliable supply that is always there, whatever the weather.
sentences.zh: 电网工程师称之为基荷电力：一种无论天气如何都始终存在、稳定且可靠的电力供应。

sentences.en: And increasingly, governments have concluded that nuclear and renewables need to work together, with nuclear providing the steady backbone that a renewable -heavy grid needs to actually function.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的政府得出结论，核能和可再生能源需要协同工作，由核能提供稳定的骨干支撑，以使以可再生能源为主的电网能够真正运转。

sentences.en: And after it's up and running, nuclear power produces almost no carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 而且在投入运行后，核能几乎不产生碳排放。

sentences.en: Now, not all Green parties agree with nuclear yet, but it's starting to change.
sentences.zh: 现在，并非所有的绿党都同意发展核能，但情况已经开始发生变化。

sentences.en: In Finland, the Green party voted back in 2022 to formally support nuclear power as part of its climate strategy, and the tone has started to change in several other countries too.
sentences.zh: 在芬兰，绿党早在2022年就投票决定，正式支持将核能作为其气候战略的一部分，其他几个国家的基调也开始发生变化。

sentences.en: So you have the energy security question and the environmental one, but there's another factor: demand for electricity is booming, and this is largely coming from the technology sitting in your pocket.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了能源安全问题和环境问题之外，还有另一个因素：电力需求正在蓬勃增长，而这很大程度上源于你口袋里的技术。

sentences.en: Data centres in the United States now use more than 4% of the country's entire electricity supply.
sentences.zh: 美国的数据中心现在消耗了该国4%以上的总电力供应。

sentences.en: A data centre is a huge building full of computer servers, the machines that store and process information for the internet.
sentences.zh: 数据中心是一栋装满计算机服务器的庞大建筑，这些机器负责为互联网存储和处理信息。

sentences.en: They've been around for decades, and despite what the fear mongering might have you believe, most of what they do has nothing to do with artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 它们已经存在了几十年，尽管某些制造恐慌的言论可能会让你产生误解，但它们的大部分工作与人工智能毫无关系。

sentences.en: They're where your Netflix movies are stored, your Spotify playlists are saved, and where the tens of billions of hours of YouTube videos are held.
sentences.zh: 它们是存储你的 Netflix 电影、保存你的 Spotify 播放列表以及存放数百亿小时 YouTube 视频的地方。

sentences.en: And yes, this episode and my voice today are brought to you courtesy of your local data centre.
sentences.zh: 没错，今天这一期节目和我的声音，也是承蒙你当地的数据中心才得以呈现给你的。

sentences.en: They are what companies talk about when they say "the cloud".
sentences.zh: 它们就是公司在谈论"云"时所指的东西。

sentences.en: It's not a cloud, it's a huge warehouse in Arizona or somewhere like that.
sentences.zh: 它不是一朵云，而是位于亚利桑那州或类似地方的巨大仓库。

sentences.en: And for most of the last twenty years, these buildings have been growing steadily but predictably.
sentences.zh: 在过去20年的大部分时间里，这些建筑一直在稳定但可预测地增长。

sentences.en: Then came generative AI which, as I'm sure you know, or might remember from episode 585, has much more intensive energy requirements.
sentences.zh: 随后出现了生成式人工智能，正如你肯定知道的，或者可能还记得第585期节目中所说的，它对能源的需求要密集得多。

sentences.en: And with billions of people using AI, well, you get a level of electricity demand that didn't really exist five years ago.
sentences.zh: 随着数十亿人使用人工智能，电力需求达到了五年前根本不存在的水平。

sentences.en: To put it in real terms, Goldman Sachs now projects that electricity demand from data centres will grow by 160% by 2030, driven largely by AI.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，Goldman Sachs 目前预测，在人工智能的推动下，到2030年，数据中心的电力需求将增长160%。

sentences.en: It means that within a few years, the amount of power these buildings need could be more than double what it is today, on top of everything else the grid has to supply.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在几年内，这些建筑所需的电量可能会比现在翻一倍还多，而这还是在电网必须供应的其他所有电力之外。

sentences.en: These data centres need reliable, 24/7 energy.
sentences.zh: 这些数据中心需要可靠、全天候不间断的能源。

sentences.en: Technology companies have actually been some of the world's biggest buyers of wind and solar power for years, but renewables alone cannot promise power at every hour of every day.
sentences.zh: 多年来，科技公司实际上一直是全球风能和太阳能的最大买家，但仅靠可再生能源无法保证每天每时每刻都有电。

sentences.en: And, one more thing. Even once a data centre is built and ready to be turned on, you don't just plug it into the grid.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事。即使数据中心建好并准备启用，你也不能直接把它插到电网里。

sentences.en: There are long waiting lists to ensure that a new customer won't overload the local network, and in some parts of the United States, these waiting lists stretch to eight years, which is eight years too long if you're a technology company racing to build the next generation of AI.
sentences.zh: 为了确保新客户不会使当地网络过载，排队等待的时间很长。在美国的某些地区，这些排队时间长达八年，如果你是一家竞相构建下一代人工智能的科技公司，八年时间实在太长了。

sentences.en: So the world's biggest technology companies did something unexpected, or I guess rather obvious when you understand that electricity is their biggest constraint.
sentences.zh: 因此，世界上最大的一些科技公司做了一件出人意料的事，或者说，当你明白电力是他们最大的制约因素时，这其实是显而易见的。

sentences.en: They decided to become energy companies themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们决定自己成为能源公司。

sentences.en: And here, enter stage right, nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，核能登场了。

sentences.en: Microsoft, for example, signed a deal back in 2024 to bring one of the two reactors at Three Mile Island, in Pennsylvania, back to life.
sentences.zh: 例如，Microsoft 早在2024年就签署了一项协议，让位于宾夕法尼亚州三哩岛（Three Mile Island）的两个反应堆之一重新启用。

sentences.en: As you may remember, Three Mile Island was the site of a famous partial meltdown back in 1979, but that happened in the other reactor.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，三哩岛是1979年著名的部分堆芯熔毁事故发生地，但那发生在另一个反应堆。

sentences.en: This one ran safely for decades, and only closed in 2019, for ordinary financial reasons.
sentences.zh: 这一个反应堆安全运行了数十年，直到2019年才因普通的财务原因关闭。

sentences.en: The plant's owner, an energy company called Constellation, is spending $1.6 billion to refurbish it, and Microsoft has agreed to buy 100% of the electricity the plant produces for the next twenty years.
sentences.zh: 该电站的所有者——一家名为 Constellation 的能源公司，正斥资16亿美元对其进行翻新，而 Microsoft 已同意在未来20年内购买该电站生产的100%电力。

sentences.en: In other words, it effectively gets its own nuclear reactor, and all of the energy it produces is earmarked for data centres.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它实际上拥有了自己的核反应堆，其产生的所有能源都专用于数据中心。

sentences.en: And it's a similar thing with Meta, Amazon, Google, all the big tech companies.
sentences.zh: Meta、Amazon、Google 等所有大型科技公司的情况也类似。

sentences.en: Some are restarting old plants, others are buying capacity from existing plants, others are investing in companies building small modular reactors, which are, as the name suggests, smaller reactors that are built off-site and then assembled, a bit like IKEA furniture, but with, I trust, slightly more helpful instructions.
sentences.zh: 有些公司正在重启旧电厂，有些公司正在从现有电厂购买容量，还有些公司正在投资建造小型模块化反应堆的公司。顾名思义，这种反应堆体积更小，在厂外制造然后进行组装，有点像 IKEA 家具，但我相信其说明书会更有用一些。

sentences.en: Add it all together, and the nuclear capacity now committed to data centres by these companies is up to 13 gigawatts, and that is just in the United States.
sentences.zh: 加在一起，这些公司目前承诺用于数据中心的核电容量高达13吉瓦，而这仅仅是在美国。

sentences.en: To put it in context, this is more electricity than the entire Netherlands uses in a year.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，这比整个荷兰一年的用电量还要多。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if that sounds like a lot or not.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这听起来算不算多。

sentences.en: It's a lot when you think that it's like the electricity used by 18 million people, but if you think that this is powering products used by a large proportion of the world's population, perhaps it seems more reasonable.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到这相当于1800万人消耗的电量，那确实很多；但如果你想到这正在为世界上大部分人口所使用的产品提供动力，也许这就显得更合理了。

sentences.en: In any case, never before has so much private money been committed to nuclear energy, and we are only six years into the decade.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，以前从未有如此多的私人资金投入到核能领域，而这十年才刚刚过去六年。

sentences.en: For decades, nuclear power depended almost entirely on governments: government funding, government regulation, government risk-taking, because private investors found it too expensive and too slow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，核能几乎完全依赖政府：政府资金、政府监管、政府承担风险，因为私人投资者觉得它太贵、太慢。

sentences.en: Now it's Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Google that are bankrolling reactors, providing the money that governments once did.
sentences.zh: 现在，是 Microsoft、Meta、Amazon 和 Google 在资助反应堆，提供了政府曾经提供的资金。

sentences.en: These are companies whose main business has nothing to do with electricity.
sentences.zh: 这些公司的主要业务与电力毫无关系。

sentences.en: But the alternative is running out of power to sell their own products.
sentences.zh: 如果不这样做，他们就会面临没有电力来销售自己产品的境地。

sentences.en: Of course, not everyone is comfortable with that shift.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有人都能坦然接受这种转变。

sentences.en: Critics point out that decisions made about something as safety-critical as nuclear power are increasingly being made by companies whose main interest is keeping their data centres running, not public accountability.
sentences.zh: 批评人士指出，针对核能这种关系到安全的关键事物所做出的决策，正越来越多地由那些主要利益在于维持其数据中心运行、而非对公众负责的公司来做出。

sentences.en: Now, there are a few more things to talk about.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有几件事需要谈谈。

sentences.en: Firstly, the financing of nuclear plants.
sentences.zh: 首先是核电站的融资问题。

sentences.en: One of the big criticisms of nuclear power, historically at least, is that it is expensive.
sentences.zh: 至少从历史上看，对核能的一大批评就是它太昂贵了。

sentences.en: Sure, once you get a plant up and running, it's cheap to run, but the build of it is incredibly expensive, and costs almost always overrun, or perhaps spiral out of control would be a better way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 当然，一旦电站建成并投入运行，其运行成本很低，但建造过程却极其昂贵，而且成本几乎总是超支，或者用"失去控制"来形容可能更贴切。

sentences.en: That is still true, but there are a few things worth mentioning.
sentences.zh: 这依然是事实，但有几点值得一提。

sentences.en: If banks and investors provide you with €1 billion in financing at a 10% interest rate, let's say, that's €100 million in interest payments every year.
sentences.zh: 假设银行和投资者为你提供10亿欧元的融资，利率为10%，那么每年仅利息支出就达1亿欧元。

sentences.en: Let's say, for the sake of example, a nuclear power plant takes 10 years to build, you will pay €1 billion in interest payments on a €1 billion loan.
sentences.zh: 举例来说，如果一座核电站需要10年才能建成，那么你为这笔10亿欧元的贷款将支付10亿欧元的利息。

sentences.en: And the numbers are often much worse than that.
sentences.zh: 而实际数字往往比这还要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: In 2016, the UK approved a nuclear power station called Hinkley Point C, in the south-west of England.
sentences.zh: 2016年，英国批准了位于英格兰西南部的一座名为 Hinkley Point C 的核电站。

sentences.en: Now, plans had actually started for this plant as early as 1981, but that's another issue.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这座电站的规划早在1981年就开始了，但那是另一个问题。

sentences.en: Anyway, its initial projected cost was £18 billion, and it was expected to come online in 2025.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，其最初的预计造价为180亿英镑，预计于2025年上线。

sentences.en: As of today, mid-2026, its projected cost is £48 billion in inflation-adjusted terms, and it's not scheduled to come online before 2030.
sentences.zh: 截至今天（2026年中期），经通胀调整后，其预计造价已达480亿英镑，且预计在2030年之前不会上线。

sentences.en: There are a few things to talk about here then.
sentences.zh: 那么，这里有几件事需要探讨。

sentences.en: The first is that big technology companies are still investing in nuclear energy despite these frequent cost overruns, which gives you some idea of just how desperate they are for power.
sentences.zh: 第一，尽管成本经常超支，大型科技公司依然在投资核能，这让你对他们对电力的渴望程度有所了解。

sentences.en: And the second is that governments are now stepping in to help the financing of new nuclear power stations, guaranteeing the price for a set period, or offering a more manageable interest rate.
sentences.zh: 第二，政府现在正介入帮助新型核电站的融资，在一定时期内保证价格，或者提供更易承受的利率。

sentences.en: And small modular reactors, which I mentioned a few minutes ago, are another way to fight the issues that have plagued the construction of these large nuclear power plants.
sentences.zh: 我几分钟前提到的小型模块化反应堆，是解决一直困扰这些大型核电站建设问题的另一种途径。

sentences.en: The fact that they are smaller means they are cheaper to build, faster to put up, and easier to place close to where the electricity is actually needed, like right next to a data centre.
sentences.zh: 它们体积更小，这意味着建造费用更低、搭建速度更快，并且更容易安置在实际需要电力的地方，比如直接建在数据中心旁边。

sentences.en: At least, that's the idea. This is still new technology, largely a technology of blueprints and prototypes rather than working power stations.
sentences.zh: 至少，想法是这样的。这仍然是一项新技术，在很大程度上还处于蓝图和原型阶段，而不是实际运行的发电站。

sentences.en: But 2026 has been the year SMRs, the small modular reactors, they started to look real.
sentences.zh: 但2026年是 SMR（即小型模块化反应堆）开始变得现实的一年。

sentences.en: There's an SMR in China which is scheduled to start commercial operation in the next 12 months, and others being built in Canada and America.
sentences.zh: 中国有一个 SMR 计划在未来12个月内开始商业运营，加拿大和美国也在建造其他 SMR。

sentences.en: Still, we'have heard this kind of story before.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们以前也听过类似的故事。

sentences.en: Nuclear power has a long history of projects that were promised on time and on budget, and then arrived years late and billions over.
sentences.zh: 核能项目的历史源远流长，它们总是承诺按时按预算完成，但最后却迟到了好几年，超支了数十亿。

sentences.en: Sceptics point out that SMRs are, so far, mostly a story told in press releases and government funding announcements, not in electricity actually flowing onto the grid.
sentences.zh: 怀疑论者指出，SMR 大多只是新闻发布会和政府资金公告里的故事，而不是真正流入电网的电力。

sentences.en: And there's also the question that has haunted nuclear power for seventy years: nuclear waste.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个困扰了核能70年的问题：核废料。

sentences.en: Anyone who grew up watching The Simpsons probably remembers Homer walking into his job at a nuclear power plant, and there being big drums of fluorescent green slime that gives fish three eyes.
sentences.zh: 任何看着《The Simpsons》长大的人可能都记得 Homer 走进他在核电站的工作岗位，那里有大桶大桶的荧光绿色黏液，会让鱼长出三只眼睛。

sentences.en: Of course, spent nuclear fuel is dangerous, and it remains radioactive for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 当然，乏燃料是危险的，并且在数千年内都保持着放射性。

sentences.en: But there has been significant investment and progress in solving this issue.
sentences.zh: 但在解决这一问题上已经有了重大的投资和进展。

sentences.en: Recently, Finland has shown that the problem can be solved.
sentences.zh: 最近，芬兰表明这个问题是可以解决的。

sentences.en: It is in the final stages of opening a nuclear storage site deep underground that will be able to safely store nuclear waste for 100,000 years.
sentences.zh: 它正处于在地下深处启用一个核存储库的最后阶段，该存储库将能够安全地储存核废料长达10万年。

sentences.en: And there is also the promise, or at least the allure, of nuclear fusion, the other kind of nuclear power, the one that works by fusing atoms together rather than splitting them apart.
sentences.zh: 还有核聚变的承诺，或者至少是它的诱惑力。这是另一种核能，它通过将原子融合在一起而不是将它们分裂来工作。

sentences.en: Fusion has been "twenty years away" for about seventy years, and 2026 hasn't quite broken that pattern.
sentences.zh: 大约70年来，核聚变一直被认为"还有20年就能实现"，而2026年也未能打破这一规律。

sentences.en: But something has changed here too. More than fourteen billion dollars in investment has gone into fusion companies, and almost a third of that arrived in the past year alone.
sentences.zh: 但这里的情况也发生了一些变化。已有超过140亿美元的投资流向了核聚变公司，其中几乎三分之一是仅在过去一年里到账的。

sentences.en: Microsoft has signed a deal to buy fusion electricity from a company called Helion by 2028.
sentences.zh: Microsoft 已经签署了一项协议，到2028年从一家名为 Helion 的公司购买核聚变电力。

sentences.en: And regulators in the US have started treating fusion as a properly separate category from traditional nuclear power, with lighter rules, because a fusion reactor can't melt down the way a fission reactor can.
sentences.zh: 美国的监管机构已开始将核聚变视为与传统核能完全不同的类别，并适用更宽松的规则，因为核聚变反应堆不会像裂变反应堆那样发生熔毁。

sentences.en: If nuclear fusion can work, and clearly there is a lot of smart money betting that it can, the economics of nuclear power change significantly.
sentences.zh: 如果核聚变能够成功，而且显然有很多聪明资金在赌它能成功，那么核能的经济学将发生重大变化。

sentences.en: In a traditional nuclear power station, the fuel keeps producing heat even after the reactor has been switched off, and it has to be kept cool at all times.
sentences.zh: 在传统的核电站中，即使在反应堆关闭后，燃料也会继续产生热量，必须时刻保持冷却。

sentences.en: At Fukushima, the reactors had already shut themselves down, but the cooling failed, and the fuel melted.
sentences.zh: 在福岛，反应堆已经自动关闭，但冷却系统失效，导致燃料熔毁。

sentences.en: This is why fission plants need so many layers of safety systems, and those layers are a big part of what makes them so expensive to build.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么裂变电厂需要如此多层的安全系统，而这些安全系统正是导致其建造费用如此昂贵的重要原因。

sentences.en: A fusion reaction has the opposite problem: it is incredibly difficult to keep going.
sentences.zh: 核聚变反应则面临相反的问题：它极难维持。

sentences.en: It only happens under extreme conditions, and there is only ever a tiny amount of fuel in the machine.
sentences.zh: 它只在极端条件下发生，而且机器中的燃料量始终微乎其微。

sentences.en: If anything goes wrong, the conditions collapse and the reaction simply stops.
sentences.zh: 如果发生任何故障，条件就会崩溃，反应就会直接停止。

sentences.en: There is nothing that can melt down. That's a large part of why people are so excited about fusion: in theory, it offers something close to nuclear power's upside, of abundant, low-carbon electricity, without its biggest danger.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西会发生熔毁。这在很大程度上解释了为什么人们对核聚变如此兴奋：理论上，它提供了接近核能的优势——充足、低碳的电力，却不带其最大的危险。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, even a couple of years ago, nuclear power was a story about a fight between the past and the future: old reactors closing in Europe while new ones opened in Asia.
sentences.zh: 总之，即使在几年前，核能还是一个关于过去与未来之争的故事：欧洲关闭旧反应堆，而亚洲开启新反应堆。

sentences.en: Today, it's a story about the environment and about energy sovereignty, not just for governments but for big tech too.
sentences.zh: 如今，这是一个关于环境和能源主权的故事，不仅对政府如此，对大型科技公司也是如此。

sentences.en: The promise is alluring: cheap, clean, abundant electricity for everyone.
sentences.zh: 这一承诺非常诱人：为每个人提供廉价、清洁、充足的电力。

sentences.en: Whether that can really be delivered, well, that is the trillion-dollar question.
sentences.zh: 至于这是否真的能实现，嗯，这就是那个价值万亿美元的问题了。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the unexpected return of nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 好的，以上就是今天关于核能意外回归的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是一期有趣的内容，并且你学到了一些新知识。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在可以评论的地方收听，请在下方评论区告诉我。对于我们的会员，你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他求知欲强的听友们畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
